correctness.rationale: Walsh eigenspace restriction is exactly the set of w-column binary syndromes. Complement and pair-XOR ranks give the universal bound. The simplex Gram has two explicitly computed eigenvalues; the unimodal binomial-ratio inequality c>N|b_w| yields full interior rank. The positive-rate dissipative spectral decomposition gives the dark space and maximal mixed-state capture law. Exact finite cross-checks: 24 independent Walsh ranks, 24 Gram ranks, exhaustive 2696 full-rank \(N=7\) generator multisets, 400 random \(N=15\) generators and one direct \(N=7\) Krylov rank. Finite checks are supporting, not substitutes for infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural physical resource-allocation problem is to maximize eventual coherent capture by exactly 2^m structured absorbers. The theorem determines the exact optimum among all affine m-dimensional trap placements, not just a single code example; the simplex construction attains the bound with a full energy-resolved spectrum. This links coding geometry, controllability, spectral degeneracy and long-time dissipative transport in an infinite family. Its distinct objective and sharp all-affine comparison are not a routine numerical table or a renamed known parameter.
